c.tagline: Chile's neocolonial beach city and gateway to the star-filled Elqui Valley.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis (black with yellow roofs) are metered; colectivos are shared fixed-route taxis with a set fare shown on the windshield. Uber, Cabify and DiDi also operate.

emergency.note: 133 reaches Carabineros (police), 131 is SAMU ambulance, and 132 is firefighters.

avoid.reason: Avoid Las Compañías and the streets around the bus terminal late at night, where robberies are reported.
Watch belongings at La Recova market and on Avenida del Mar beaches; car break-ins occur at beach parking lots.

hood_desc: The neocolonial old town around the leafy Plaza de Armas, packed with restored churches, craft markets, museums and pedestrian streets - the best base for sightseeing and staying central.
The 3 km beachfront esplanade lined with aparthotels, cabañas, seafood restaurants and bars facing the Pacific; ideal for a relaxed beach stay in summer, though a short taxi ride from downtown.
The area around the iconic Faro Monumental lighthouse where Avenida del Mar meets the historic center, blending easy beach access with walkable proximity to town.
A quiet residential district between the center and the coast, with local markets, guesthouses and an authentic everyday feel at lower prices.
A beach and resort sector stretching toward neighboring Coquimbo, home to the Enjoy casino-resort, long sands and family cabañas; calm and car-friendly but away from La Serena's old town.
lodging: Enjoy Coquimbo Hotel de la Bahía

water.note: City tap water is safe to drink, though some prefer bottled for taste.

transit.pay: Pay the flat fare in cash to the driver on micros and colectivos - roughly CLP 500-800 (~$0.55-0.90) per ride. There is no rechargeable transit card; carry coins and small notes.
transit.hours: Micros and colectivos run roughly 6am to 10-11pm; taxis and ride apps cover later hours.
transit.note: La Serena has no metro; buses, colectivos and taxis cover the city, and it links to neighboring Coquimbo by frequent micros. The compact historic center is easily walked.

bus: Micros & colectivos to Coquimbo and the Elqui Valley

transit.m: Taxi or transfer to the center, ~10-20 min
Colectivo/micro from the main road to downtown, ~20-30 min

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants (often suggested on the bill as 'propina'); optional but expected for table service.

food.name: Pastel de jaiba
food.desc: Crab meat baked in a clay dish with bread soaked in milk, butter and cheese until bubbling; the north's comfort food and La Serena's signature plate.

places.name: Fogon del Mar
places.note: Seafood house repeatedly singled out for its pastel de jaiba and chupe.

places.name: Restaurante Bakulic
places.note: Beachfront classic serving pastel de jaiba, caldillo de congrio and ceviche.

places.name: Recova Marina, Caleta San Pedro
places.note: Fishermen's food court with a row of stalls doing crab pie and paila marina.

food.name: Empanadas de mariscos
food.desc: Fried or baked pastries stuffed with prawn and cheese, machas or crab; the coastal answer to the inland pino beef empanada.

places.name: Recova Marina, Caleta San Pedro
places.note: Machas-and-cheese empanadas fried to order beside the fishing boats.

places.name: Mercado La Recova
places.note: Upstairs comedores in the covered market sell empanadas all day.

places.name: Casa Campo Ulriksen
places.note: Known for its empanadas as much as its grilled meat and seafood.

food.name: Caldillo de congrio
food.desc: Conger eel simmered with potato, onion, tomato and white wine into the fragrant fish stew Neruda wrote an ode to; served scalding in a clay bowl.

places.name: Restaurante Bakulic
places.note: Long-running seaside dining room where caldillo is a menu fixture.

places.name: Recova Marina, Caleta San Pedro
places.note: Simple stalls, very fresh fish, unbeatable value for a full caldillo.

food.name: Chupe de locos and mariscos
food.desc: Chilean abalone or mixed shellfish baked in a rich bread-and-cheese gratin, close cousin to pastel de jaiba but deeper and more savoury.

places.name: Fogon del Mar
places.note: Chupe de jaiba and shellfish gratins are the reason locals drive out here.

places.name: Recova Marina, Caleta San Pedro
places.note: Chupe de locos when the season and the divers allow it.

food.name: Papaya de La Serena
food.desc: The small, intensely perfumed local papaya, poached in syrup and eaten in almibar, as jam, in juice or over ice cream; the city's edible emblem.

places.name: Mercado La Recova
places.note: Whole floor of stalls selling papaya in syrup, jam and sweets; taste before buying.

places.name: Shops around the Plaza de Armas
places.note: Traditional sweet shops sell boxed papaya confites to take home.

food.name: Chumbeque
food.desc: Layered northern Chilean biscuit sandwiched with papaya or mango jam and dusted with sugar; a Norte Grande sweet sold across the Coquimbo region.

places.name: Mercado La Recova
places.note: The obvious place to find chumbeque alongside papaya sweets and alfajores.

places.name: Shops around the Plaza de Armas
places.note: Sweet counters in the old centre stock chumbeque by the piece or boxed.

food.name: Pisco sour
food.desc: Chilean pisco distilled in the Elqui Valley just inland, shaken with lime, sugar and ice; the region produces the grapes and the spirit.

places.name: Restaurante Bakulic
places.note: Sundown pisco sour with the Pacific in front of you.

places.name: Destileria Pisco Mistral
places.note: Day trip inland for tastings at the source; tours run most of the year.

places.name: Planta Capel
places.note: Big Elqui distillery with a visitor centre and guided tastings.

food.name: Mote con huesillo
food.desc: Chile's summer street drink: a dried peach rehydrated in sweet spiced syrup with a scoop of husked wheat at the bottom, eaten with a spoon.

places.name: Plaza de Armas vendors
places.note: Carts under the trees on the main square from late morning in summer.

places.name: Avenida del Mar beachfront
places.note: Vendors work the beach promenade on warm afternoons.

landmarks: Faro Monumental
La Serena's beloved 1950s lighthouse, a crenellated white-and-red landmark standing where Avenida del Mar meets the long Pacific beach.
Catedral de La Serena and Plaza de Armas
The limestone neoclassical cathedral of 1844 presides over a palm-shaded colonial plaza at the heart of Chile's second-oldest city.
La Recova Market
The city's craft and food market, arcaded courtyards fragrant with papaya sweets where vendors sell alpaca knits, lapis lazuli and Diaguita-inspired pottery.
Museo Arqueológico de La Serena
An archaeology museum treasuring Diaguita ceramics, Atacama mummies and an original Easter Island moai brought from Rapa Nui.
Avenida del Mar
A six-kilometer beachfront boulevard of wide sands, seafood restaurants and cycle paths sweeping south from the lighthouse toward Coquimbo.
Iglesia San Francisco
A fortress-like stone church begun around 1600, considered one of Chile's oldest surviving churches and a jewel of colonial religious architecture.
Jardín del Corazón (Japanese Garden)
South America's largest Japanese garden, a serene composition of koi ponds, bridges and pines commemorating friendship between Chile and Japan.
Barrio Inglés
A former English merchant quarter near the port with weathered façades and a hillside mural, offering views over La Serena's colonial rooftops and the bay.
Casa González Videla
An 1892 house on the Plaza de Armas that belonged to president Gabriel González Videla, now a museum of regional history and period furnishings.
Iglesia Santo Domingo
A limestone colonial church dating to 1755 near the Plaza de Armas, notable for its later, eclectic bell tower rising above La Serena's historic centre.

train.note: There is no passenger railway serving La Serena - EFE's network does not extend this far north and Chile's only international train is the Arica-Tacna line. Arrive by coach on Ruta 5 or fly into La Florida airport.

bus.note: No international coaches from La Serena - the Argentine crossings are further south at Santiago or north at Antofagasta. The terminal south of the centre has Turbus (https://www.turbus.cl/) and Pullman services to Santiago in about 6 hours and north to Antofagasta and Arica, plus local buses to Coquimbo and up the Elqui Valley to Vicuña and Pisco Elqui.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry from La Serena or neighbouring Coquimbo - the port handles cargo. Boat trips from Punta de Choros to the Humboldt penguin reserve at Isla Damas, about two hours north, are wildlife excursions.

half.name: Elqui Valley
half.blurb: A luminous valley of vineyards and pisco distilleries winding into the Andes, famed for poet Gabriela Mistral and some of Earth's clearest skies.

full.name: Mamalluca Observatory
full.blurb: A purpose-built public observatory near Vicuña where nightly tours reveal the southern sky's nebulae and galaxies through powerful telescopes.

full.name: Humboldt Penguin National Reserve
full.blurb: Boat excursions from Punta de Choros circle Isla Damas and Choros to see penguins, dolphins, sea otters and sometimes whales in turquoise water.
